consensus_findings.description: Scaffold generator lower-cased the first letter of the acceptance outcome, producing 'The system SHALL ensure that pRs created by /autopilot ...' (the 'PRs' acronym became 'pRs'). The requirement text is still readable but is wrong as written and will propagate into the merged capability spec on sync.

The proposal's Selected Approach section says design.md records decisions '(D1–D13)', but design.md now has D14 (solo-mode suppression of unowned_* findings) added in plan iteration 1, and the proposal itself cites D14 elsewhere. The readiness checklist in plan-findings.md correctly says D1–D14.

The YAML front-matter comment states 'merges and every failure/escalation path still wait for a human', but `replan_required` (which fires when a roadmap item enters replan_required, a failure-adjacent path) is set to `auto`. The prose table below does explain that replan_required is covered by roadmap approval, so the posture is internally justified, but the header comment, which is what an operator reads first when editing the gates, overstates what blocks.

All 19 scaffolded spec deltas satisfy the WHEN/THEN rule only mechanically: every scenario is 'WHEN `<change>` is implemented THEN <restated requirement>', which is tautological and untestable, and all of them target the placeholder capability directory `multiplayer-collaboration`. The files are clearly marked as plan-roadmap scaffolds to be refined by /plan-feature, and the ownership-map change shows what the refined form looks like, so this is expected at this stage, but syncing any of these scaffolds as-is would add vacuous requirements to a placeholder capability.

checkpoint.json commits a dispatch `launch_token` and lease `owner_nonce` into the tracked repository. These are one-shot launch-gate markers for an already-resolved attempt (lease state 'released', outcome 'parked'), and the same pattern is already tracked for the dispatch-governance and principal-credential-architecture roadmaps, so there is no live credential exposure; flagged only so the convention is a conscious one.

The `PathPattern` schema regex admits an embedded `**` (e.g. `openspec/spec**s/`) and also sequences like `***`, relying on the loader to reject them per design D3. The split is documented in both the schema description and D3, and the spec has a scenario for the loader half, so this is a deliberate two-layer validation rather than a gap; noting it because schema-only validators (e.g. an editor plugin) will accept a value the resolver refuses.
